Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:151056

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 32538 of 2024
Applicant :- Jatin Nagpal

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Deepak Singh,Jitendra Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,R.S. Maurya
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Heard Sri Jitendra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri R.S. Maurya, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.106 of 2024, under Sections 420, 408 IPC, Police Station Medical College, District Meerut,
during pendency of the trial.

entities.text: Police Station Medical College, District Meerut
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and co-accused Mayank Kaushik and according to the FIR, applicant was the Assistant Manager in the company of the informant and he along with co-accused who was the Manager, was posted at a petrol pump for the purpose of sale of a product and by playing fraud since 2022-2023, applicant and co-accused embezzled about Rs.27 Lakhs and this fact came into knowledge of the informant after the Audit Report.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation levelled against the applicant is totally false and actually, some dispute with regard to the non-payment of the salary of the applicant Jatin Nagpal vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75886503/
1 arose between applicant and informant and only due to this reason applicant has been falsely made accused in the present matter.
5.

sentences.text: He further submits that when relationship of the applicant and informant was cordial one then through his sister, applicant has taken some loan from the informant and in this regard, he also give certain amount to the informant and the fact that amount of Rs.11 Lakhs has been given by the applicant and other co-accused is admitted by the informant in his statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

He further submits that even this fact is reflected from the complaint filed by the informant under the provisions of N.I. Act.
6.

He next submits that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class with maximum punishment of seven years and applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 11.07.2024.

7. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that after the detailed Audit Report, it was revealed that applicant and co-accused duped the informant and embezzled about Rs.27 Lakhs and out of Rs.27 Lakhs, some of the amount was also returned by them and this fact shows that both committed fraud and cheating and applicant failed to provide any cogent explanation with regard to the Audit Report.
8.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. However, as per allegation, applicant along with co-accused duped the informant and embezzled more than Rs.27 Lakhs being his employee but it reflects that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate-I Class with maximum punishment of seven years and applicant is not having any previous criminal history.
10. Further, law is settled that bail application should not be dismissed for punitive purpose.
11. Further, bail is a rule and bail rejection is an exception and until proven guilty an accused deemed to be innocent.
12. Further, in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 11.07.2024.

13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant - Jatin Nagpal be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
